judgements.reason: ContourIntegration is fully built in TauCeti/Analysis/Contour (HW Thm 3.3, the homology Cauchy theorem, generalized winding numbers), so nothing is missing; PolynomialGaloisGroups still needs the resolvent factorization theorem with the quartic and quintic tables, Jordan's p-cycle theorem, the n ≤ 5 transitive-group classification with certificates, the imported Dedekind cycle-type theorem and S_n over ℚ.

DirichletPadicLFunctions must first import p-adic analysis well beyond Mathlib's Amice transform (completed group rings, φ/ψ, pseudo-measures, locally analytic distributions with rigid weight spaces) and Tate zeta integrals, then build Kubota–Leopoldt, all-character measures, Leopoldt's formula and Eisenstein measures; PolynomialGaloisGroups' remaining resolvent, classification and certificate work sits on an already built orbit/block/discriminant/resolvent base with only a small Dedekind-theorem import.

HopfRinow already has the Levi-Civita connection, geodesic spray, maximal geodesic intervals and the manifold inverse function theorem, and lacks the exponential map, Gauss lemma, minimizing geodesics and the Hopf–Rinow implications; DirichletPadicLFunctions lacks all five of its own layers plus imported pseudo-measures and completed group rings, locally analytic distributions and Tate's thesis.

ComplexComparisonPartII needs complex analytic spaces and analytification (absent from the library), Oka coherence and Cartan–Serre cohomology, projective and proper GAGA with imported Hilbert–Quot schemes and algebraic spaces, Chow's theorem and the algebraic de Rham comparison; HopfRinow's remaining exponential map, Gauss lemma, minimizing geodesics and Hopf–Rinow theorem form one textbook chapter on built Riemannian foundations.

Besides the circle method itself (van der Corput, Vinogradov mean values via decoupling, Waring, three primes, Birch) and zero-density analytic number theory, ExponentialSums imports through FF.2 the Weil conjectures and Deligne's Weil I–II with Lefschetz pencils, étale duality and the étale-cohomology foundations; ComplexComparisonPartII's analytic-space base, Oka/Cartan theory, GAGA, Chow and de Rham comparison with algebraic spaces (R09.1–R09.3) is a much smaller stack.

Both share the étale-duality foundations and the curve Weil estimate (EDC.0–EDC.3, DWP.0–DWP.1, abelian schemes); on top, ExponentialSums needs Deligne's Weil I–II (DWP.2–DWP.7), Lefschetz pencils and vanishing cycles, the Weil conjectures, explicit-formula and large-sieve theory and the circle method with decoupling, whereas FunctionFieldArithmetic adds function-field class field theory, Bruhat–Tits buildings and parahorics, Satake and automorphic forms over K, with its Riemann–Roch layer already largely built in Tau Ceti.

FunctionFieldArithmetic needs étale duality and the curve Weil estimate, abelian schemes and algebraic stacks, function-field class field theory and Chebotarev, Bruhat–Tits theory, Satake and automorphic forms over K (about 50 unshared layers); AdicSpacesPartII needs the unfinished adic-space sheaf theory, formal and rigid geometry (fibre products, Raynaud fibres, Kiehl coherence), dagger spaces, étale sites and perfectoid spaces with almost purity (about 20 unshared layers).

AnabelianGeometry imports AdicSpacesPartII F0, R0–R3 and R5 inside its p-adic Hodge theory stack (perfectoid P0–P6, diamonds, AInf, crystalline and prismatic comparison) and adds complex GAGA, Poitou–Tate duality, Coleman integration, the étale fundamental group, anabelian reconstruction and Chabauty–Kim theory, while AdicSpacesPartII's only unshared parts are dagger geometry and the étale-site re-export.

Both import the same p-adic Hodge, perfectoid and étale stack; beyond it Faltings adds Shimura varieties with canonical models, toroidal compactifications and PEL moduli, char-0 resolution, Néron models and Arakelov/Faltings heights before its own isogeny-estimate and Tate-conjecture layers, while AnabelianGeometry adds Poitou–Tate duality, p-adic measures, Coleman integration, étale fundamental groups and Chabauty–Kim theory.

FaltingsFiniteness imports ShimuraCompactifications C0–C5 together with almost all of its Shimura-variety, PEL and GAGA prerequisites, and adds the whole p-adic Hodge theory stack, Néron models, Arakelov heights and its own finiteness proofs; the parts unique to ShimuraCompactifications (general-data canonical models V7/V8.general, Hilbert H0–H4, C6) are small by comparison.

HeckeStacks rests on the Fargues–Scholze machinery — the relative Fargues–Fontaine curve, Bun_G, geometric Satake with fusion, v-stack/solid/lisse sheaves and diamond six operations — on top of perfectoid spaces, étale cohomology with Deligne weights and Bruhat–Tits theory (about 180 unshared layers), whereas ShimuraCompactifications' unshared stack is Shimura varieties, PEL/Hilbert moduli, GAGA and toroidal/Faltings–Chai compactification (about 60).

ModularIwasawaMainConjectures imports about 600 layers — Kato and Heegner Euler systems, automorphic congruences, p-adic families, modularity lifting and Serre/potential modularity, Shimura varieties and compactifications, Faltings, p-adic L-functions and p-adic Hodge theory — while only geometric Satake, Bun_G, v-stack sheaves, isocrystal bundles and its own five layers (about 40) are unique to HeckeStacks.

ModularIwasawaMainConjectures' imports contain most of TorsionCohomology's (Shimura varieties and compactifications, perfectoid and étale stacks) plus about 300 further layers (Euler systems, modularity and patching, p-adic families, Faltings, Iwasawa cohomology); TorsionCohomology's unshared part is completed cohomology, Borel–Serre, perfectoid Shimura varieties, the Hodge–Tate period map and its own five layers (about 45).

ContourIntegration is complete in the baseline, whereas HopfRinow still lacks the smooth geodesic flow and exponential map, normal neighbourhoods and the Gauss lemma, minimizing geodesics and first variation, and the Hopf–Rinow equivalence.

TorsionCohomology shares AnabelianGeometry's p-adic Hodge and perfectoid base and adds about 200 unshared layers (Shimura varieties and compactifications, perfectoid Shimura varieties and the Hodge–Tate period map, completed cohomology, endoscopic transfer with the fundamental lemma, Galois representations for CM fields); AnabelianGeometry's unshared part (Poitou–Tate, Coleman integration, étale π₁, reconstruction, Chabauty–Kim) is about 33 layers.

ContourIntegration has nothing missing; DirichletPadicLFunctions needs pseudo-measures and completed group rings, locally analytic distributions with rigid weight spaces and Tate zeta integrals, and its own Kubota–Leopoldt, all-character, Leopoldt-formula and Eisenstein-measure layers.

Unshared, ShimuraCompactifications needs Shimura varieties with Baily–Borel, Borel extension (with char-0 resolution) and canonical models via CM theory and Milne's conjugation, PEL and Hilbert moduli, complex GAGA, Dieudonné/Breuil–Kisin and perfectoid basics, then toroidal and Faltings–Chai compactification; ExponentialSums' unshared stack — étale foundations with Deligne's Weil I–II, Lefschetz pencils and the Weil conjectures, plus analytic number theory and the circle method — is similarly deep but somewhat smaller.

TorsionCohomology shares HeckeStacks' perfectoid, diamond, étale and Deligne-weight foundations and adds about 170 unshared layers (Shimura varieties and compactifications, completed cohomology, Borel–Serre, endoscopic transfer and the trace formula, perfectoid Shimura varieties, Galois representations for CM fields); HeckeStacks' unshared part is geometric Satake, Bun_G, v-stack sheaves, isocrystal bundles and its five own layers (about 40).

ModularIwasawaMainConjectures imports all of FaltingsFiniteness' layers R28.1–R28.6 with their whole prerequisite stack (through elliptic-curve modularity) and adds about 400 further layers: Euler systems, automorphic congruences, modularity lifting, p-adic families and Iwasawa cohomology.

Both are analytic comparison foundations; AdicSpacesPartII needs the unfinished Huber sheaf theory, formal schemes and Raynaud fibres, rigid GAGA and Kiehl coherence, dagger spaces, étale sites and imported perfectoid spaces with almost purity plus an ∞-categorical derived-sheaf layer, which outweighs ComplexComparisonPartII's analytic-space base, Oka/Cartan coherence, GAGA and Chow with Hilbert–Quot schemes and algebraic spaces, and the de Rham comparison.

HopfRinow's remainder is a stacked new theory — smooth geodesic flow on TM and the exponential map, normal neighbourhoods and the Gauss lemma, minimizing geodesics and first variation, then the Hopf–Rinow implications; PolynomialGaloisGroups' remainder (resolvent factorization and quartic/quintic tables, Jordan's p-cycle theorem, the n ≤ 5 classification with certificates, S_n over ℚ, and a Dedekind theorem whose ingredients are largely in Tau Ceti) is broader but shallower on an already built dictionary.

AnabelianGeometry imports the full p-adic Hodge theory stack (AInf, crystalline, prismatic, perfectoid spaces, diamonds, relative Fargues–Fontaine), complex GAGA, Poitou–Tate duality and Coleman integration before its own reconstruction and Chabauty–Kim layers (about 140 unshared layers); FunctionFieldArithmetic's unshared part is function-field class field theory, Bruhat–Tits theory, Satake and the curve Weil estimate (about 19).

ExponentialSums needs the circle method with decoupling, explicit-formula and zero-density theory and, through FF.2, Deligne's Weil I–II with the étale-cohomology foundations (about 84 layers, none shared); DirichletPadicLFunctions needs p-adic measures and pseudo-measures, locally analytic distributions and Tate's thesis before its own five layers (about 21).

ModularIwasawaMainConjectures imports ShimuraCompactifications C0–C6 with all their Shimura-variety prerequisites and far more (Euler systems, congruences, modularity, p-adic families, Faltings, p-adic Hodge theory); only the general-data interfaces V7, V8.general, C2.general and C3.general are unique to ShimuraCompactifications.
